**TL;DR**
Jim Fan argues that robotics is undergoing "The Great Parallel" to the LLM playbook, transitioning from language-heavy models to World Action Models (WAM) trained on massive egocentric video datasets and neural simulations, aiming to pass the physical Turing test within 2–3 years.

## The Great Parallel: Copying the LLM Success
Jim Fan proposes that robotics is currently "speedrunning" the same four-stage evolution that defined Large Language Models (LLMs) between 2020 and 2026.

*   **The Four Stages:**
    *   **Pre-training (2020/GPT-3):** Learning the "grammar" of the world; for robots, this is simulating the next physical state.
    *   **Alignment/Fine-tuning (2022/InstructGPT):** Shaping the simulation to perform useful, specific work.
    *   **Reasoning (2024/o1):** Using Reinforcement Learning (RL) to surpass simple imitation learning.
    *   **AutoResearch (2026/Expected):** Accelerating the loop through autonomous agents and swarm collaboration.
*   **The Shift to World Action Models (WAM):** Fan argues that current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are "head-heavy" on language but "physics-light" on verbs and spatial reasoning.
    *   **DreamZero:** Nvidia’s new model that "dreams" a few seconds into the future, decoding next world states and motor actions simultaneously to solve zero-shot tasks.
    *   **Physics Emergence:** By predicting pixels at scale, models like Veo-3 naturally learn gravity, buoyancy, and visual planning without explicit coding.

## Scaling Data: From Tele-op to Egocentric Video
The "bottleneck" in robotics is the data flywheel. Fan identifies a shift away from traditional, non-scalable collection methods.

*   **The Death of Tele-operation:** Traditional tele-op is capped by the 24-hour physical limit of a robot/human pair and is often inefficient and slow.
*   **Sensorized Human Data:**
    *   **Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI):** Wearable robot actuators that allow humans to collect data without the robot body in the loop.
    *   **DexUMI:** An exoskeleton designed by Nvidia that maps human hand movements to 5-finger dexterous robot hands, enabling 1:1 data collection.
*   **EgoScale (The FSD Equivalent):** This model uses human egocentric (POV) videos as its primary "diet."
    *   **Scalability:** Nvidia pre-trained EgoScale on 21,000 hours of human video with 0% robot data, using only 4 hours of tele-op for final alignment.
    *   **The Scaling Law:** Fan identified a clean log-linear relationship between pre-training hours and validation loss for dexterity, similar to language model scaling laws.

## Environments as Data: Neural Simulation
To reach the scale of 1 million environments, robotics must move beyond physical hardware into digital space.

*   **The Equation:** Fan asserts that "Compute = Environment = Data." The more compute available for simulation, the more data the model generates autonomously.
*   **Real-to-Sim-to-Real:** Using consumer devices like iPhones as "pocket world scanners" to turn physical objects into interactive 3D assets inside physics simulators.
*   **DreamDojo (Neural Simulators):** A purely data-driven simulator that takes actions as input and outputs RGB frames and sensor states. 
    *   It bypasses classical physics equations and graphics engines entirely, learning the "mechanics" of a robot from data.

## The Robotics Roadmap to 2040
Fan outlines three major achievements remaining on the "technology tree" for robotics to reach its endgame.

*   **The Physical Turing Test (2–3 Years):** Reaching a state where a robot's labor is indistinguishable from a human’s in terms of energy in vs. unit labor out.
*   **The Physical API:** Creating standardized command-line interfaces for robot fleets, enabling "lights-out factories" that function as "printers of atoms" to output fully assembled products from markdown files.
*   **Physical AutoResearch (By 2040):** The final stage where robots design and build the next generation of themselves, far surpassing human capabilities.

> "The main diet for robotics will be egocentric videos... We're able to break the curse of 24 hours per robot per day." — **Jim Fan**

> "Our generation was born too late to explore the earth and too early to explore the stars, but we're born just in time to solve robotics." — **Jim Fan**

> "If you believe in robotics, robotics will believe in you." — **Jim Fan** (referencing Ilya Sutskever)

briefings.title: Sam Altman in conversation with Patrick Collison
briefings.tldr: OpenAI is entering its third phase as a "mega-scale token factory for the world," aiming to become a low-margin, high-volume infrastructure utility that accelerates global economic output and scientific discovery.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
OpenAI is entering its third phase as a "mega-scale token factory for the world," aiming to become a low-margin, high-volume infrastructure utility that accelerates global economic output and scientific discovery. Sam Altman predicts that AI will soon move beyond coding to automate the "drudgery" of all computer-based work, while significantly compressing the timeline for breakthroughs in material science and biotechnology.

## The Evolution of OpenAI’s Mission and Strategy
* **Three Phases of OpenAI:** Sam Altman outlined the company’s structural trajectory:
    * **Phase 1:** A pure research lab focused on the "crazy" goal of building AGI.
    * **Phase 2:** The development of a product-focused company (ChatGPT, APIs).
    * **Phase 3:** A global "token factory" providing massive-scale intelligence as a new public utility.
* **The "Infrastructure Play":** Altman views OpenAI’s future as an infrastructure provider similar to Stripe, favoring a low-margin, high-volume business model aligned with customer success.
    * **Switching Costs:** He notes that as AI gets smarter, switching costs between models actually decrease, making high-margin "moats" harder to maintain and further incentivizing the utility model.
* **Massive CapEx Requirements:** Altman describes the current build-out as the most expensive infrastructure project in human history.
    * **Demand vs. Price:** He believes demand for intelligence is effectively uncapped, provided the price continues to drop and speed increases.
    * **Bubble Concerns:** While journalists frequently call a "CapEx bubble," Altman argues that the current scale of demand makes the massive investments look reasonable.

## Product Frontiers: From Coding to "General Drudgery"
* **The Coding Threshold:** The recent "parabolic" growth in AI utility was triggered by models hitting a reasoning threshold that made them effective for coding.
    * **Codex and OpenClaw:** These tools represent a shift where the AI becomes the primary interface for the computer. 
    * **Automation of Drudgery:** The next major unlock isn't a specific domain like spreadsheets, but the automation of "switching between apps" and "copy-pasting"—the small tasks that break creative flow.
* **"Revenge of the Idea Guys":** In the startup ecosystem, technical talent remains vital, but the barrier to entry has lowered.
    * **Founder Traits:** Altman is now more willing to fund "idea-driven" founders who deeply understand their users but may lack traditional coding skills, as AI handles more of the technical execution.
* **Headcount Projections:** Despite the massive scale of the business, Altman expressed a desire to keep OpenAI’s headcount extremely lean, ideally only doubling from its current size over the next five years.

## Science and the OpenAI Foundation
* **Accelerating Discovery:** Altman believes the most important contribution of AI will be accelerating science, potentially achieving a decade’s worth of progress in a single year.
* **The OpenAI Foundation:** This non-profit arm will be one of the largest foundations in the world, focusing on science and AI resilience.
    * **Material Science:** Altman identified this as the most underrated domain for AI impact, noting its potential to revolutionize catalysts and physical materials.
    * **Biotech and Health:** OpenAI is supporting efforts like the Arc Institute to tackle complex diseases (e.g., Alzheimer’s) through foundation models like Evo-2.
* **Energy Breakthroughs:** Altman made the bold prediction that the world may see a profitable nuclear fusion reactor within the next five years, driven partly by the massive energy demands of AI data centers.

## Management Style and Philosophy
* **Hands-Off Leadership:** Altman describes himself as a non-hands-on manager who hires great people, gives them a high-level goal, and stays out of the way. 
    * **Context Gathering:** He maintains a "pulse" on the company by communicating with hundreds of employees daily via Slack/text to gather diffuse context.
* **Managing Elite Talent:** The "magic" of OpenAI was getting highly capable, often iconoclastic individuals to work together long enough to reach breakthroughs. This was achieved through a shared, deep conviction in "scale" and concentrating resources on a single research program.
* **Iterative Deployment vs. Power Concentration:** Altman defended OpenAI’s decision to release tools like ChatGPT early and often. 
    * He rejects the "ivory tower" approach where a small group of experts controls the technology, arguing instead for democratized access so the world can build on it.

> "We have to figure out how to build this like mega, mega scale token factory for the world... we need to make that as smart, as cheap, as abundant, as easy to use as possible." — Sam Altman

> "I think we're going to try this new experiment where we start sending like an FTE to work... hands-on with the CEO of a company to automate their job as much of it as they can." — Sam Altman

> "The most important contribution of AI... is that if we can start to discover new science at a much faster rate... life gets better because we understand science better." — Sam Altman

briefings.title: Siemens & Adidas CEOs über Digitale Fertigung, KI und Innovation in der Industrie
briefings.tldr: The integration of industrial AI, digital twins, and 3D printing is dramatically accelerating manufacturing speeds and enabling mass-personalization, though German bureaucracy and high energy costs pose significant risks to European competitiveness against the rapid scaling seen in China and the US.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The integration of industrial AI, digital twins, and 3D printing is dramatically accelerating manufacturing speeds and enabling mass-personalization, though German bureaucracy and high energy costs pose significant risks to European competitiveness against the rapid scaling seen in China and the US.

## Industrial AI & The Digital Twin Strategy
* **Digital Twin Efficiency:** Siemens CEO Roland Busch highlighted that creating digital replicas of products and factories reduces development cycles from 40 months to 20 months or less.
    * **Impact:** This approach yields 20–30% (and up to 50%) time savings and significantly increases energy efficiency and variability.
* **AI Agents in Programming:** Siemens has launched AI "engineering agents" that can autonomously write and validate control software.
    * **Productivity Gains:** This technology reduces manual workload by 50% and increases code quality by 80% compared to traditional human engineering.
* **Predictive Maintenance:** In modern "smart" buildings, AI agents monitor occupancy and sensor health to optimize temperature and lighting, moving from scheduled maintenance to a "need-based" model.

## The Future of Sports Performance & Manufacturing
* **Hyper-Personalization:** Bjørn Gulden (Adidas) predicts that within 5 to 10 years, consumers will scan their feet in-store to receive 100% custom-produced shoes, moving away from standard sizing.
* **3D Printing (Additive Manufacturing):** Adidas is currently producing "4D" shoes that are fully automated and printed without handwork. 
    * **Technological Limits:** While current 3D printing is slower and more expensive than mass production, it allows for innovations like the 97-gram marathon shoe that can improve professional run times by four minutes.
* **AI in Marketing:** Adidas is already shifting toward "synthetic" (AI-generated) models for e-commerce photography to save time and cost, though major stars like Lionel Messi will remain "real."

## Global Competition & The "China Factor"
* **Scaling Advantage:** China leads globally in scaling new technologies. While a single machine might print a shoe in Germany, China deploys "football fields" of 3D printers to drive costs down.
* **Local-for-Local Strategy:** Geopolitical pressures and shifting tariffs (especially in the US) are forcing companies toward decentralized production. 
    * **Market Differences:** China’s consumers prioritize digital integration and "car-as-a-living-room" features, whereas European markets are fragmented across 26 different regulatory environments.
* **Battery Tech Dominance:** Busch noted that China has effectively "decoupled" from the rest of the world in lithium-ion battery technology and supply chain ecosystems.

## Workforce Transformation & Cultural Shifts
* **The Death of Coding:** Roland Busch stated that "software is solved," meaning the role of the traditional coder is being replaced by "Architects" who manage AI agents to write code 100,000 times faster.
* **Skills Over Roles:** Humans will not necessarily be replaced by AI, but by "humans who can operate AI." Adidas is focusing on "Prompting" as a vital new professional skill.
* **Leadership as a Marathon:** Both CEOs emphasized physical fitness and team-sport experience as foundational for managing global corporations. Busch trains 6 days a week (primarily strength/circuits), while Gulden uses "Rollski" (roller skis) daily.
* **Education Investment:** Siemens invests €430 million annually in employee training and education to keep the workforce "future-proof" amidst the rapid 7–8 year disruption cycle of AI.

## Systemic Hurdles: Bureaucracy & Infrastructure
* **Bureaucracy Costs:** Administrative hurdles cost German industry an estimated €13 billion annually.
    * **Specific Examples:** Busch criticized "Gold-Plating" (adding extra German regulations on top of EU laws) and cited cases where individual animal protection (e.g., a single lizard) stops major infrastructure or military projects.
* **The "Leisure Gap":** Busch pointed out that Germans work an average of 400 hours less per year than the OECD average, raising concerns about the national "performance principle."
* **Infrastructure Deficit:** Bjørn Gulden noted that Norway’s sports success is due to conscious investment in school-based facilities, whereas German public building costs are 2.5x higher than private sector projects due to over-regulation.

> **Notable Quotes**
>
> "The human is the most difficult factor. 80% of your thoughts as a CEO are always about people—how to motivate them and how to change them in the face of AI and crises." — **Bjørn Gulden, Adidas CEO**
>
> "Most humans won't be replaced by AI, but by humans who know how to use AI. My advice to young people: Do not treat this as a hobby; use it productively." — **Roland Busch, Siemens CEO**
>
> "Democracy in Germany has become bureaucracy. If I read every regulation and document required for a single Saturday event, you’d simply die. We must get honest about this if we want growth." — **Bjørn Gulden, Adidas CEO**
>
> "The steam engine took 60 years to change the world; electricity took 30; the internet took 15. We are talking about 7 to 8 years for AI—and three are already gone." — **Roland Busch, Siemens CEO**

briefings.title: Stripe Sessions 2026 | Indexing the economy
briefings.tldr: The global economy is undergoing a structural "replatforming" around AI, characterized by a surge in high-revenue solopreneurship, "global-day-one" scaling for startups, and the emergence of autonomous agentic commerce supported by stablecoin infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The global economy is undergoing a structural "replatforming" around AI, characterized by a surge in high-revenue solopreneurship, "global-day-one" scaling for startups, and the emergence of autonomous agentic commerce supported by stablecoin infrastructure.

## Current Economic Indicators and Myths
* **SaaS Resilience:** Despite a $1 trillion market value loss in the software sector in January 2026, Stripe data shows SaaS payment volumes remain higher than pre-sell-off levels, indicating fundamental revenue strength.
* **Rational Markets:** Outsize valuations have shifted strictly toward the most profitable companies, correcting the "dot-com" style irrationality where unprofitable firms were highly rewarded.
* **Tariff Pass-Through:** While trade volumes remain stable, the downward price trend in durable goods (typically driven by manufacturing productivity) has reversed as businesses pass cumulative tariff costs to consumers.
* **The "K-Shaped" Myth:** Contrary to popular narratives of a wealthy-only recovery, Stripe data shows the spending gap between high-income and low-income consumers is actually shrinking.
* **Labor Market Cooling:** Recent unemployment upticks are attributed more to interest rates and "pandemic hiring hangovers" than to AI displacement.

## The Explosion of Economic Dynamism
* **Solopreneurship at Scale:** There is a massive re-acceleration in US business formations, driven primarily by "non-employer firms." Nearly 5 million Americans now earn their living as solopreneurs generating over $100,000 in revenue.
* **Accelerated Growth:** The Stripe Atlas program recently hit 100,000 incorporations. The "Class of 2026" startups are tracking to five times the revenue of the 2025 cohort at the same stage.
* **Global-by-Default Playbook:** Modern startups no longer wait to expand. The median top-100 AI startup on Stripe earns most of its revenue internationally and sells into 55 countries within its first year. 
* **Coasian Shift:** Based on Ronald Coase’s theory of the firm, AI is lowering the "coordination costs" between companies. This leads to a future of fewer people per firm, higher output per firm, and more coordination via efficient external markets.

## The Rise of Agentic Commerce
* **Evolution of Autonomy:** Commerce is moving from "Level 1" (software filling out forms) to "Level 2" (reasoning assistants like Wayfair’s shopping bot) toward "Level 5" (fully autonomous agents).
* **Machine-to-Machine Payments:** Autonomous agents are already executing micro-transactions. John Collison demonstrated an AI agent researching energy markets and autonomously purchasing four cents worth of proprietary data to complete its task.
* **Infrastructure Requirements:** To move agentic commerce into the mainstream, three layers are required:
    * **The Economic Layer:** Agents must be able to pay and businesses must accept those payments.
    * **Micropayment Viability:** For tiny, frequent transactions, stablecoins are becoming the essential infrastructure due to near-zero transaction costs.
    * **The Trust Layer:** Systems to manage permissions and verify agentic identity.

## Strategic Moats in an AI Economy
* **Complementary Assets:** As intelligence becomes cheap and abundant, its "complements" become more valuable. Key high-value assets now include:
    * **Energy and Hardware:** Massive demand for data center power is driving value for gas turbine manufacturers (e.g., Siemens Energy).
    * **Proprietary Data:** Companies like Reddit and Stripe (Radar) are monetizing data that was previously a "dormant asset" on the balance sheet.
    * **Real-World Execution:** Traditional firms like John Deere are maintaining moats through "complex interactions" between software and physical hardware (tractors in 130 countries).
* **The Productivity Lag (Solo Paradox):** Historically, transformative technologies like electricity (1882) and computing (1987) took decades to show up in productivity statistics because the economy had to "digest" and redesign itself. Collison predicts the AI "digestive" period will be significantly shorter than the 30 years required for electrification.

> "The markets are being tediously rational. The most profitable companies are the ones being rewarded with outsize valuations." — **John Collison**

> "It used to be that young companies sold mostly at home, and only ventured out to the open sea of global commerce once they'd gotten big. Now, it's the newborns on Stripe who are globe-trotting their way through the long tail of markets." — **Emily Sands**

> "Transformative technology looks for a long time like it's not doing much if you're looking at the economic gauges... but these are the early indicators of an economy that's replatforming itself." — **John Collison**

briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
At the Stripe Sessions event, key product and industry leaders detailed how the integration of AI agents, programmable command-line interfaces (CLIs), and stablecoins is driving a massive acceleration in global business creation and transforming the future of "agentic commerce."

---

## The Intersection of AI Agents and Crypto Wallets
* **Surging Developer Interest:** Approximately 35% of new sign-ups on the Web3 auth platform Privy are currently for developers building agentic wallets.
    * These wallets allow users to allocate specific spending allowances to AI agents and include "clawback" capabilities to retrieve unspent assets.
* **Micro-Payment Innovations:** Initial agentic use cases are occurring in the background, focused on business model innovations like real-time, risk-free streaming payments gated on a per-token basis.
* **Autonomous Transactions:** Over time, AI agents are expected to independently operate their own wallets across both fiat and stablecoin rails, automating B2B and B2C transactions.

## Stripe Atlas and the Rise of "Vibe Businesses"
* **Market Dominance:** Jeff Weinstein (Stripe Product Team) revealed that Stripe Atlas now incorporates approximately 26% of all new Delaware C-corporations. 
    * Atlas recently celebrated its 100,000th incorporated business, an AI startup optimizing battery usage for power plants.
* **Programmable Business Creation:** To cater to the rise of autonomous systems, Stripe is introducing new programmatic features:
    * **Atlas CLI:** A command-line interface allowing developers and AI agents to programmatically spin up C-corporations.
    * **Integrated Fundraising:** Founders will soon be able to execute full SAFE fundraising rounds directly through Atlas, generating fundraising links that deposit investor capital directly into Stripe Treasury accounts.
* **Exponential Scaling:** While it took eight years to reach the first 100,000 Atlas startups, Weinstein projects that the next 100,000 will be incorporated in just one to two years due to AI-assisted developer workflows.

## Designing Financial Infrastructure for AI Legibility
* **Agent-First Web Design:** Weinstein emphasized that to survive the shift to agentic commerce, businesses must make their platforms "legible" to LLMs.
    * **Structured Data Over UI:** Agents do not care about bright colors or heavy JavaScript; they require perfect, markdown-formatted data regarding SKUs, offers, and checkout parameters.
* **The Rise of CLI Usage:** The Stripe Command Line Interface (CLI)—originally built as a power tool for terminal purists—is now Stripe's fastest-growing interface because AI agents prefer structured code environments over navigating web dashboards.
* **Link for Agents:** Stripe's consumer-facing Link wallet is introducing features that allow users to safely delegate purchasing authority to agents (e.g., authorizing an agent to make up to $50 of purchases over a 30-minute window using FaceID or 2FA).

## Stablecoins as the Next Major Financial Platform Shift
* **Refuting the "Fizzle" Narrative:** Zach Abrams (Founder of Bridge) pushed back against claims that the stablecoin market is stagnant, noting that Bridge's transaction volumes grew 4x last year and an additional 20% month-over-month recently. 
    * **Utility Over Speculation:** While macro supply figures fluctuate with digital asset prices, non-trading utility—such as Meta using stablecoins for global creator payouts—is growing aggressively.
* **A New Payment Primitive:** Abrams compared stablecoins to the credit card boom of the 1970s. While cards became the core platform shift for the early internet, stablecoins paired with AI represent the platform shift for autonomous agents.
    * **Agentic Requirements:** Agentic commerce requires transaction velocity, micro-scale incrementality, and instant settlement finality that traditional credit card networks (with chargebacks and high transaction fees) cannot support.
* **Stripe Treasury Expansion:** To facilitate seamless global movement of funds, Stripe is scaling Stripe Treasury globally, with plans to support multi-currency storage and movement across 160 countries by the end of the year.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "You have to make your business legible to the agents... Agents want perfect information about what your offer is, what the tool is, what the SKU is, what the shoe is, and we're basically helping businesses just make their entire checkouts, their entire SKU offering legible." — Jeff Weinstein

> "Cards were this new form factor and cards combined with the internet was like 90% of all fintech... Our view was that stablecoins represented another platform shift in payments, and I think AI could be the corresponding one that helps drive adoption." — Zach Abrams

> "Now we put out a beta, developers send their agents after our beta page, they'll go around our waitlists to use it, and they'll give us feedback from their agent logs of how the agent was using our developer tools. In like minutes!" — Jeff Weinstein

briefings.title: This is AGI: Sequoia AI Ascent 2026 Keynote
briefings.tldr: Artificial Intelligence has transitioned from a revolution in communication to a revolution in computation, shifting the focus from "faster horses" (incremental productivity) to "cars" (long-horizon agents).
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Artificial Intelligence has transitioned from a revolution in communication to a revolution in computation, shifting the focus from "faster horses" (incremental productivity) to "cars" (long-horizon agents). This shift is transforming software into a $10 trillion services market where cognitive labor is being commoditized at an unprecedented scale.

## The Paradigm Shift: From Communication to Computation
Pat Grady (Partner, Sequoia) characterizes the current AI wave not as a tool for distributing information, but as a fundamental shift in how information is processed.

*   **A Revolution in Computation:** Unlike the internet or mobile waves, which focused on communication, AI is a "revolution in computation." This creates a "moving floor" where the technological foundation changes daily.
*   **Three Inflection Points:**
    *   **Pre-training:** Validated by the "ChatGPT moment" in late 2022.
    *   **Reasoning:** The emergence of inference-time scaling (e.g., OpenAI’s o1).
    *   **Long-Horizon Agents:** The arrival of agents that can persist until a job is done (e.g., Claude Code), which Grady defines as "functional AGI."
*   **The "Car" Analogy:** Previous AI applications were "faster horses" (10-40% productivity gains). The new era of agents represents "cars"—tools that offer 10-40x productivity and fundamentally change the nature of organizations.
*   **The $10 Trillion Opportunity:** AI is moving beyond the $650B software market into the multi-trillion dollar services market. For example, legal services in the US alone represent a $400B vertical that can now be addressed by AI.

## The MAD Strategy for AI Builders
Grady offers the **MAD** framework for founders building on top of foundation models to navigate a market where "no lead is safe."

*   **Moats (Customer-Back Approach):** In a world where product capabilities change instantly, moats are built by wrapping technology around the customer. While technology is vital, customer intimacy is more durable than specific features.
*   **Affordance (Path of Least Resistance):** Borrowing from design, "affordance" means creating tools that are intuitive. While a terminal (like Claude Code) is powerful, builders must create interfaces that are "brain-dead simple" for the average enterprise user.
*   **Diffusion (The Capability Gap):** The "diffusion gap" is the space between what labs can do and what Fortune 500 companies actually use. This gap represents the primary opportunity for application-layer startups.

## The Rise of the Agentic Economy
Sonya Huang (Partner, Sequoia) argues that "services is the new software," as agents move from "cute but useless" experiments to autonomous workers.

*   **The Agentic Scale:** AI is progressing through four stages of autonomy:
    1.  **AI Assistance:** Tab auto-complete and inline help.
    2.  **Agentic Development:** Humans instructing and managing agents.
    3.  **Async Agents:** Background agents spawning sub-agents with minimal human oversight.
    4.  **Dark Factories:** High-leverage systems where human review is removed entirely (already appearing in cybersecurity).
*   **Tokens vs. Salaries:** Hiring agents is infinitely more scalable and cheaper than hiring humans. Tasks that previously required expensive salaries are being replaced by token costs.
*   **Vertical Impact:**
    *   **Medicine:** Agents inspecting genomes and prescribing medication.
    *   **Law:** Agents performing litigation and settling contracts.
    *   **Science:** Agents discovering new superconductors or solving complex mathematical problems.
*   **Compressed Timelines:** The ability to stack AI-driven breakthroughs means that "whatever you could imagine building over the next 100 years is now possible in 100 days."

## The Cognitive Industrial Revolution
Konstantine Buhler (Partner, Sequoia) predicts that AI will do for cognitive work what the Industrial Revolution did for physical labor.

*   **99.9% Machine Cognition:** Just as 99% of physical work is now done by machines (planes, combustion engines), Buhler predicts nearly all cognition will eventually be machine-led.
*   **The Commoditization of Intelligence:**
    *   **The Aluminum Analogy:** In the 1800s, aluminum was more precious than gold. Once electrolysis made it easy to extract, it became disposable. Intelligence is currently "aluminum"—a precious skill that is about to become a cheap, instantly invoked commodity.
*   **Alien Design:** When machines take over design, the results will be "alien" and non-intuitive to humans. Buhler cites a NASA antenna designed by an evolutionary algorithm that outperformed human designs but lacked any recognizable geometric symmetry.
*   **The Science of AI:** We are currently in a "tinkering phase" similar to early steam engine development. Buhler predicts the emergence of a formal science of AI—comparable to thermodynamics—within the next few decades.
*   **The Human Measure:** As AI masters logic and realism, the value of work will shift toward human connection and the "Art of Unreason." Relationships and emotional experiences will become the primary measures of value.

## Notable Quotes

> "Functional AGI is when you can dispatch an agent to do a job, and it can recover from failure and persist until that job is done." — **Pat Grady**

> "The last two decades that we spent building tools for humans have ended up being able to port over to be incredibly useful for agents as well... SaaS is not dead; its value will explode as the number of agents using it increases." — **Sonya Huang**

> "We're about to enter a world where some of the most precious skills that took decades to earn—PhD-level skills—are so instantly invoked that right after using them, you can crumple them up and throw them right in the trash." — **Konstantine Buhler**

> "You cannot pass 15 cars in the sun, but you can pass 15 cars in the rain. And right now, there is a torrential downpour of new capabilities." — **Pat Grady**
